_note: Companion patterns for scan two. Regex, matched case-insensitively
against cell text and against the two governing labels.
These lists are TUNED TOWARD REPORTING ABSENCE. A pattern that is
too loose produces a false PRESENT, which removes a row from a
report whose whole subject is what is missing. A pattern that is
too tight produces a false ABSENT, which adds a row the operator
can dismiss in a second. The two costs are not symmetric, so bare
single-letter unit abbreviations (m, s, t, c, f, k) are deliberately
absent: they would match ordinary prose and silence real gaps.
A word list cannot read sense. 'range' is a variance term in one
column and a spatial extent in another, and nothing here can tell
them apart. Swap this file rather than widening the code.
2026-08-25, BEFORE any real workbook was read: the generic
parenthetical rule \((?:[a-z...][a-z0-9...]{0,14})\) was REMOVED and
replaced by a slash-parenthetical rule plus explicit energy and fuel
unit words. The generic rule fired on any short parenthetical --
'(see note 3)' read as a unit -- which is the costly direction. The
replacement is tighter there and wider on mmBtu / therm / scf / MWh /
short ton / CO2e.
TUNING DIRECTION, stated because it runs toward a prediction:
widening the unit list makes 'unit PRESENT' easier to satisfy, and
targets/EPA.md predicts unit PRESENT on the Emission Factors Hub. No
change to this list can make the VARIANCE or SAMPLE patterns fire, so
the differential in that prediction -- unit present while variance and
sample size are absent -- is not reachable by editing this file.
